title: Meta-Learned Model Selection for Heterogeneous-Goal Self-Adaptive AI Systems
research_question: Can replacing Bayesian Model Averaging in the analyze stage of a MAPE-K loop with a stacking-based meta-learner improve prediction accuracy and downstream adaptation quality when self-adaptive AI systems must satisfy heterogeneous goals such as thresholds and optimization objectives?
hypothesis: A stacking-based analyze module that learns context-dependent weights over heterogeneous predictive models will outperform Bayesian Model Averaging on both predictive accuracy and adaptation effectiveness under heterogeneous requirements, especially when no single candidate model is consistently correct.
motivation: The knowledge base identifies model-selection uncertainty in self-adaptive systems as underexplored and explicitly flags future work on extending current BMA-based approaches to additional domains and heterogeneous requirements. This creates a concrete gap: existing MAPE-K analyze modules address uncertainty with BMA, but BMA assumes the true model is among candidates and uses posterior weighting rather than learned performance-based combination. A stacking-based meta-learner is a plausible next step because it can combine diverse models adaptively and may better support AI systems facing mixed threshold and optimization goals.
